data.description:
## Description

**What**: Open a test PR that intentionally violates a rule the local gate previously caught (e.g., a critical security finding), confirm that CI-side enforcement (Ruleset checks via the parity-uplifted llm-review plus the required-checks list) blocks merge, then close the PR without merging and delete its branch in the same session.
**Why**: Epic SCs 3 and 4 require in-session, evidence-based verification that CI enforcement is operative after local gates are removed. Without this story, there is no validated proof that the CI side catches what local enforcement caught.
**Scope**:
- IN: Create a test branch with a deliberate violation (e.g., a hard-coded secret, a known-bad import, or a file with a critical security pattern); open a PR targeting main; poll `gh pr checks` until the check completes and confirms the relevant check fails; confirm `gh pr merge --auto` is queued but not executing due to the failed check; close the PR without merging via `gh pr close`; delete the test branch via `git push origin --delete`; verify the PR state via `gh pr view --state all` shows CLOSED.
- OUT: Modifying CI workflow definitions (3aaa-0238), changing enforcement.strategy config (5428-bebd), implementing the merge primitive (8787-ac16).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a test PR with a deliberate violation has been opened on this repo and `gh pr checks` confirms the relevant CI check failed — verified in-session with the actual check output recorded as a ticket comment
  ← Satisfies: sc-3 "CI-side enforcement blocks merge — verified in-session via gh pr checks showing the failed check and gh pr merge --auto queued but not executing"
- When this story is complete, the deliberate-violation PR is closed without merging and its branch deleted, confirmed via `gh pr view --state all` showing state CLOSED — verified in-session with the actual gh output recorded as a ticket comment
  ← Satisfies: sc-4 "PR is closed without merging and its branch deleted in the same session — verified in-session via gh pr view --state all showing state CLOSED"
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The deliberate violation PR must be explicitly closed (not abandoned) — autoclose-on-stale or merge-queue flush could accidentally merge it if not explicitly closed in-session
- [Security] The bad change introduced for testing must be obvious and intentional (e.g., a string with 'password=test123' or equivalent) — use a pattern the LLM review security overlay is documented to catch
- [Testing] This story is itself a validation story; the primary evidence is in-session output captured as ticket comments, not unit tests on new logic

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an agent, I can confirm CI enforcement blocks a deliberate-violation PR and clean up afterward
